title: The Otto cycle: how compression ratio sets a petrol engine's efficiency
examples: How does compression ratio affect efficiency?
Why can petrol engines not use very high compression?

parts.label: Spark plug
parts.ask: What does the spark plug do?

explain.say: In 1876 Nikolaus Otto built the first practical four-stroke engine, and billions of petrol engines still follow his idea: suck, squeeze, bang, blow. Look at one cylinder: valves at the top, a spark plug, and a piston turning the crankshaft. Engineers model its gas with an ideal loop called the Otto cycle.

draw.text: Four strokes: intake, compression, power, exhaust

explain.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a petrol engine cylinder. Look at the piston, the valves and the spark plug. The Otto cycle is a simple model of what happens in here. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: The Otto cycle: how compression ratio sets a petrol engine's efficiency

explain.say: Start at the bottom right, with the cylinder full: half a litre of air at 100 kilopascals. The piston squeezes it adiabatically to a tenth of the volume, so the pressure climbs to about 2500 kilopascals. Then the spark fires and the heat arrives almost instantly, at constant volume. See the pressure shoot straight up?

It triples, to about 7500 kilopascals! Next the power stroke: the hot gas expands adiabatically and drives the piston down. At the bottom the exhaust valve opens and the pressure drops at constant volume, carrying heat away. The area inside the loop is the work of one cycle. Which stroke gives the work?

draw.text: Heat in at constant volume, heat out at constant volume

explain.say: The power stroke! Now the key result: the efficiency depends only on the compression ratio. Eta equals 1 minus 1 over r to the power gamma minus 1. At r equals 8 that is 56.5 percent; at 10 it rises to 60.2 percent. See the curve climb and then flatten? What stops us using r equals 20?

curves.label: Air-standard Otto
curves.ask: How does compression ratio affect efficiency?

explain.say: Knock! Squeeze petrol and air too hard and the mixture self-ignites before the spark, hammering the piston. So petrol engines stay around 10 to 13 to one. Real engines reach only about 30 to 40 percent, because of friction, heat loss and real gases. Great job! Challenge: what is the ideal efficiency at r equals 12?

curves.label: Air-standard Otto
curves.ask: How does compression ratio affect efficiency?

faq.a: The ideal air-standard cycle for spark-ignition engines: adiabatic compression, heat added at constant volume, adiabatic expansion, and heat rejected at constant volume.
asks: what does the Otto cycle P-V diagram show

faq.q: What does the spark plug do?
faq.a: It ignites the compressed fuel–air mixture at the top of the compression stroke. The burning is so fast that the cycle models it as heat added at constant volume.

faq.q: How does compression ratio affect efficiency?
faq.a: Higher compression ratio means higher efficiency: eta equals 1 minus 1 over r to the power gamma minus 1. The gains get smaller as r grows.

faq.q: Why can petrol engines not use very high compression?
faq.a: At high compression the mixture gets so hot that it ignites by itself before the spark, called knock, which damages the engine. Higher-octane fuel resists knock.

faq.q: Why are real engines less efficient than the Otto cycle?
faq.a: Real engines lose heat to the cylinder walls, have friction and pumping losses, burn fuel in a finite time and use real gases whose properties change with temperature.

facts: Nikolaus Otto built the first practical four-stroke internal combustion engine in 1876.
The air-standard Otto efficiency is 1 minus 1 over r to the power gamma minus 1.

quiz.say: An air-standard Otto cycle has a compression ratio of 9. With gamma equals 1.4, what is its efficiency?
quiz.show: Otto cycle, r = 9, γ = 1.4. Ideal efficiency?

wrong.1: That is 1 over r to the 0.4, the fraction rejected.
wrong.2: That is 1 minus 1 over r, without the power gamma minus 1.

quiz.say: In the ideal Otto cycle, how is heat added?
quiz.show: In the ideal Otto cycle, heat is added at…
quiz.why: Combustion after the spark is modelled as instant, so the piston has no time to move.

wrong.1: Constant pressure heat addition is the Diesel cycle.
wrong.2: Constant temperature heat addition belongs to the Carnot cycle.
